MetaCyc:PWY-6823

The complete eight-reaction native route is represented for the Escherichia coli K-12 protein core: MoaA cyclizes GTP, MoaC forms cPMP, sulfur-carrier activation and recycling supply both sulfurs of molybdopterin, and Mog/MoeA adenylation and molybdate insertion yield Mo-molybdopterin. The sulfur-transfer net reaction retains five whole protein carrier states and a generic reductant; it does not specify every elementary relay. YnjE enhances reconstitution without a claim of universal indispensability. MoaA cyclase/cluster assignments retain their HAMAP inference, while direct MoaC experiments distinguish the E. coli enzyme from Staphylococcus aureus MoaA used in coupled assays. Native assemblies concern MG1655 within K-12; individual kinetic and genetic experiments have narrower strain and assay scopes. Anaerobic nitrate-respiration complementation and oxygen-sensitive radical-SAM preparations do not imply exclusive anaerobic pathway operation. The endpoint is unmodified Mo-MPT, before MCD or bis-MGD synthesis and cofactor insertion into target enzymes. The initial PathBank map also includes a separate folate branch and MocA cytidylation; those are outside this exact native boundary. Alternative sulfur-donor compensation, tungsten substitution, and high-molybdate bypass conditions do not establish uniform wild-type flux.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:3:The new record is **MetaCyc:PWY-6823, molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis**, at `data/pathways/molybdenum-cofactor-biosynthesis.yaml`. It represents all eight reactions in the inspected MetaCyc 22.5 pathway, including cysteine desulfuration, MoaD activation and sulfur recycling, and ends at unmodified Mo-molybdopterin. The selected protein core is **Escherichia coli K-12 (NCBITaxon:83333)**. Native assemblies are curated for MG1655, within that scope; individual experimental strains and assay readouts are narrower. This is a reaction-level pathway, not a claim that every transient enzyme intermediate or physiological electron donor is known.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:5:The initial PathBank lead **SMP0001902 / PW001888.owl** is not an exact equivalent. ./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:3:The new record is **MetaCyc:PWY-6823, molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis**, at `data/pathways/molybdenum-cofactor-biosynthesis.yaml`. It represents all eight reactions in the inspected MetaCyc 22.5 pathway, including cysteine desulfuration, MoaD activation and sulfur recycling, and ends at unmodified Mo-molybdopterin. The selected protein core is **Escherichia coli K-12 (NCBITaxon:83333)**. Native assemblies are curated for MG1655, within that scope; individual experimental strains and assay readouts are narrower. This is a reaction-level pathway, not a claim that every transient enzyme intermediate or physiological electron donor is known.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:13:PathBank 5153 uses the same thiocarboxylated carrier on both sides and has inconsistent carrier counts. Current Rhea instead consumes two thiocarboxylated MoaD equivalents and regenerates two carboxy-MoaD equivalents. The native RXN-8342 releases four protons, whereas current Rhea releases two for its explicit chemistry. Native RXN-8348 consumes a proton and produces water; current Rhea instead releases a proton and describes Mo(VI)O2(OH)-MPT. The old CPD-8123 CML is MoO2-MPT, C10H10MoN5O8PS2, charge −2, even though it carries the same CHEBI:71302 cross-reference. Current ChEBI/Rhea describes C10H11MoN5O9PS2, charge −4. These formal chemical representations are not treated as identical, nor as direct measurements of the intracellular redox/ligand state. Current balanced Rhea chemistry is the selected graph representation.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:15:The five RHEA-COMP identifiers retain whole IscS and MoaD carrier states. Formula checks use their native `reactivePart` formula to cancel the unchanged protein backbone, without replacing the graph nodes by isolated residues. Both formal AH2/A redox pairs remain generic. Dithionite or DTT used in reconstitution is not declared the physiological electron donor. The net sulfur-transfer reaction does not duplicate its component transformations as a second route.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:19:Nine reviewed K-12 proteins are included: MoaA P30745, MoaC P0A738, MoaD P30748, MoaE P30749, MoeA P12281, MoeB P12282, Mog P0AF03, IscS P0A6B7 and YnjE P78067. P30747 is a demerged accession; its organism-specific successors are not interchangeable. The K-12 MoaC entry is P0A738.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:21:The six independently identified native assemblies are the MoaC hexamer (CPLX-8331), MoaD2-MoaE2 synthase (CPLX0-2502), MoeB homodimer (CPLX0-8164), Mog homotrimer (CPLX0-8163), MoeA homodimer (CPLX0-8045), and IscS homodimer (CPLX0-248). Every component coefficient and native monomer-to-UniProt cross-reference is replayed. The Thermus complex CPLX-8334 is excluded. A transient MoeB2-MoaD2 complex is described as a substrate-associated catalytic state, not invented as an additional externally identified species. Current MoaA annotation reports monomer/homodimer; its functional `enables` edge does not claim isolated-monomer sufficiency.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:25:Full PMID:19946146 supports IscS-specific interaction and sulfur delivery in the tested E. coli system, while also documenting in vitro donation by CsdA and SufS and residual activity in deletion strains. PMID:21856748's inspected primary abstract supports **YnjE enhancement** in a defined IscS/MoeB/MoaD reconstitution. It does not demonstrate isolated YnjE catalysis of the complete net reaction or universal in vivo necessity. YnjE's separate thiosulfate reaction is not mistaken for this role. Its periplasmic annotation and the uncertain cellular relay prevent a blanket compartment assertion. TusA's pleiotropic, condition-dependent effects in PMID:23281480 are retained as context rather than a chemically resolved direct MoaD-transfer edge.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-nicotine-next/moco-curation.md:27:PMID:12571226 supports the two-MoaD-per-cPMP stoichiometry and MoaD/MoaE synthase architecture. Current UniProt directly cites experimental evidence for MoeB adenylation, Mog adenylation and MoeA insertion. PMID:15632135 used purified E. coli proteins and human apo-sulfite oxidase as a readout; the latter is not an E. coli pathway catalyst. Its thiol inhibition differs from older extract-dependent assays, so no glutathione-consumption or obligatory glutathione-cofactor edge is added. Tungsten substitution and high-molybdate bypasses remain condition-specific context.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-pathways/thiamine-scout-handoff.md:5:* **Molybdenum cofactor from GTP, PathBank:SMP0001902 / PW001888.owl**, member SHA-256 `629f85741809eb0e420762fd0b59154c43888870c37f39743fd07fb02deb07ae`. Ten source reactions combine a GTP-to-pterin branch with molybdenum-cofactor formation. Reaction 5152 assigns GTP-to-cPMP to MoaA alone; MoaC requires independent disposition. Reaction 5153 uses the same thiocarboxylated MoaD form on both sides with different coefficients. Reaction 3398 lacks a controller. MocA Q46810 retains an old uncharacterized-name label. A future task must establish the exact canonical full boundary and whole-carrier chemistry, not simply accept these source mappings.

MetaCyc:PWY-6823

The complete eight-reaction native route is represented for the Escherichia coli K-12 protein core: MoaA cyclizes GTP, MoaC forms cPMP, sulfur-carrier activation and recycling supply both sulfurs of molybdopterin, and Mog/MoeA adenylation and molybdate insertion yield Mo-molybdopterin. The sulfur-transfer net reaction retains five whole protein carrier states and a generic reductant; it does not specify every elementary relay. YnjE enhances reconstitution without a claim of universal indispensability. MoaA cyclase/cluster assignments retain their HAMAP inference, while direct MoaC experiments distinguish the E. coli enzyme from Staphylococcus aureus MoaA used in coupled assays. Native assemblies concern MG1655 within K-12; individual kinetic and genetic experiments have narrower strain and assay scopes. Anaerobic nitrate-respiration complementation and oxygen-sensitive radical-SAM preparations do not imply exclusive anaerobic pathway operation. The endpoint is unmodified Mo-MPT, before MCD or bis-MGD synthesis and cofactor insertion into target enzymes. The initial PathBank map also includes a separate folate branch and MocA cytidylation; those are outside this exact native boundary. Alternative sulfur-donor compensation, tungsten substitution, and high-molybdate bypass conditions do not establish uniform wild-type flux.
